> [!NOTE] > ## Reviews paused > > It looks like this branch is under active development. To avoid overwhelming you with review comments due to an influx of new commits, CodeRabbit has automatically paused this review. You can configure this behavior by changing the `reviews.auto_review.auto_pause_after_reviewed_commits` setting. > > - Last reviewed commit: 1e05486c21d56fbcbc64dd397461837c0eeb6a9e > - Latest commit, not reviewed: 43c2b4c5e551e05f4d10e27388991709ce35fffa > > Use the following commands to manage reviews: > - `@coderabbitai resume` to resume automatic reviews. > - `@coderabbitai review` to trigger a single review. > > Use the checkboxes below for quick actions: > - [ ] ▶️ Resume reviews > - [ ] 🔍 Trigger review
📝 Summary
## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Route-weight publishing now requires a valid, positive source version and at least one task with valid evidence. Regressions in previously evidenced tasks are held for 24 hours; recovery clears the hold, and a changed set of regressing tasks restarts it. * Capacity-only changes can publish immediately when task evidence is unchanged. The regression override bypasses only the partial-regression hold. * Export logs include the resolved feedback database and source version. Refused publish attempts display their logs. * **Documentation** * Updated route-weight export guidance to describe publication checks, hold behavior, and provenance logging. The exporter resolves its feedback database, logs source provenance, and checks task evidence before publishing. It holds partial evidence regressions for 24 hours, supports an override for those holds, and refuses invalid or wholly unevidenced output. Tests and documentation cover database selection, publication decisions, and cadence failure reporting. **Changes: Route-weight export** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Feedback database resolution**
`src/feedback.py`, `src/route_weights_export.py`, `tests/test_route_weights_export.py`, `tests/test_route_weights_publication.py`, `docs/ROUTE_WEIGHTS_EXPORT.md`|The CLI resolves the feedback database using the configured path precedence and uses it to build the local export. It logs the resolved path and source version. Tests cover path selection, URI characters in database paths, and build failures.| |**Evidence guard and publication**
`src/route_weights_export.py`, `tests/test_route_weights_export.py`, `tests/test_route_weights_export_cli.js`, `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/ROUTE_WEIGHTS_EXPORT.md`, `.verify-floor.json`|Publication rejects invalid source versions and all-false evidence. It holds partial task-evidence regressions for 24 hours, with an override limited to that hold. It checks the fetched remote artifact and includes database, version, and author details in changed-document commits. Tests cover refusals, allowed publications, malformed remote artifacts, and provenance.| |**Cadence failure reporting**
`orchestrate.sh`, `tests/test_route_weights_export.py`, `tests/test_firing_regressions_section.py`, `tests/test_route_weights_publish_cadence.py`|The cadence step prints the captured export log when publication fails. Tests check failure reporting and update publisher mocks to accept keyword arguments.| **Priority:** ➖ Normal **Estimated code review effort:** 3 (Moderate) | ~30 minutes **Change:** Bug fix · **Severity of issue fixed:** Medium ### Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant ExportCLI as route_weights_export.py CLI participant DBResolver as feedback.resolve_db_path participant Publisher as publish_document participant Remote as Remote export branch participant Guard as publish_guard ExportCLI->>DBResolver: Resolve feedback database path DBResolver-->>ExportCLI: Return resolved path ExportCLI->>Publisher: Submit document and publication options Publisher->>Remote: Fetch published artifact Remote-->>Publisher: Return artifact Publisher->>Guard: Check proposed and published documents Guard-->>Publisher: Return publication decision Publisher->>Remote: Commit changed document when allowed ```
Merge Risk: 🔵 Low · up to 1e054
The publication guard now handles most malformed remote states cleanly. A remote artifact with a malformed task_types field can still crash a cadence run with a traceback instead of a clean refusal. The new database-resolution logic also needs a module selftest. Both are small fixes to make before or soon after merge.

The current `_require_publishable()` publishes that partial regressio… | Keep every partial evidence regression refused unless `--allow-evidence-regression` is set, or update issue [`#660`] to approve timed automatic publication. Add or update tests for the required behavior and rerun `python3 src/verify.py`. | | Docstring Coverage | ![Warning](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/pre-merge-checks-warning.svg) | Docstring coverage is 23.81% which is insufficient. The publisher test-double updates and capacity-only ev… | | Title check | ![Passed](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/pre-merge-checks-passed.svg) | The title clearly and concisely describes the main change: adding evidence guards to route-weight export. | | Description check | ![Passed](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/pre-merge-checks-passed.svg) | The description is directly related to the changeset. It explains shared database resolution, publication guards, evidence regression handling, validation results, and remaining acceptance items. |
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check
**Explanation** The changed resolver, route-weight guard, hold and override tests, cadence refusal logging, provenance, and documentation implement issue [`#660`]. The publisher test-double updates and capacity-only evidence-preservation tests support those publication requirements. No unrelated change is demonstrated.
Full details: Linked Issues check
**Explanation** Issue [`#660`] requires refusal when a previously evidenced task becomes unevidenced unless `--allow-evidence-regression` is passed. The current `_require_publishable()` publishes that partial regression automatically after the 24-hour hold when the flag is absent. The resolver, provenance logging, absolute refusals, cadence reporting, tests, and documentation address the other coding requirements. The PR reports a green CI-shaped verification run, but live publication and mirror readback are non-coding follow-up tasks. **Resolution** Keep every partial evidence regression refused unless `--allow-evidence-regression` is set, or update issue [`#660`] to approve timed automatic publication. Add or update tests for the required behavior and rerun `python3 src/verify.py`.
Full details: Docstring Coverage
**Explanation** Docstring coverage is 23.81% which is insufficient. The required threshold is 80.00%. Docstring coverage is scoped to functions touched by this diff. Analyzed 42 functions across 8 files. (1 skipped: 1 unsupported.) **Resolution** Write docstrings for the functions missing them to satisfy the coverage threshold.

performed_via_github_app.description:
# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues
